answer_text:
Using the Taylor expansion at \(z=0\),

\[
1-\cos z=\frac{z^2}{2}-\frac{z^4}{24}+\frac{z^6}{720}-\cdots
=\frac{z^2}{2}\left(1-\frac{z^2}{12}+\frac{z^4}{360}-\frac{z^6}{20160}+\cdots\right).
\]

Thus

\[
f(z)=\frac{1}{1-\cos z}
=\frac{2}{z^2}\left(1-\frac{z^2}{12}+\frac{z^4}{360}-\cdots\right)^{-1}.
\]

Inverting the bracketed series gives

\[
\left(1-\frac{z^2}{12}+\frac{z^4}{360}-\cdots\right)^{-1}
=1+\frac{z^2}{12}+\frac{z^4}{240}+\frac{z^6}{6048}+\cdots.
\]

Therefore,

\[
f(z)=\frac{2}{z^2}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{z^2}{120}
+\frac{z^4}{3024}+\frac{z^6}{86400}+\cdots.
\]

Since there is no \(1/z\) term, the residue at \(z=0\) is \(0\).

\[
\boxed{
\frac{1}{1-\cos z}
=
\frac{2}{z^2}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{z^2}{120}
+\frac{z^4}{3024}+\frac{z^6}{86400}+O(z^8),
\qquad
\operatorname{Res}_{z=0}\frac{1}{1-\cos z}=0
}
\]
